messages.subject: c-hat value and model selection
parts:
Dear distance sampling list,

I'm applying CTDS, and Im applying the two-step procedure described by Howe et al 2019 to select the best model.

In the second step, I obtained c-hat values close to one (specifically, 0.66, 1.06, and 1.94)

If I'm right,
- chat = 1 indicates no overdispersion  
- chat > 1 indicates overdispersion, and higher chats, more overdispersion


Does it mean that the two-step procedure should not be applied to my data because data are not overdispersed? thus, the AIC (traditional procedure) should be applied?

I copied here the results of my analysis (just in case it helps).

-- TWO-STEP PROCEDURE --
STEP-1:

> QAIC(uni1, uni2, uni3)
     df     QAIC
uni1  1 107.6461
uni2  2 112.0566
uni3  3 110.0247

> QAIC(hn0, hn1)
    df     QAIC
hn0  1 176.1893
hn1  2 177.3494

> QAIC(hr0, hr1)
    df     QAIC
hr0  2 232.2622
hr1  3 234.2625

STEP-2:

|modnames                                                                   | chats|
|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----:|
|hazard-rate key function                                            |  0.66|
|half-normal key function                                            |  1.06|
|uniform key function with cosine(1) adjustments |  1.94|

-- TRADITIONAL AIC PROCEDURE --

> AIC(uni1, uni2, uni3)
     df      AIC
uni1  1 197.5204
uni2  2 204.0677
uni3  3 198.4619

> AIC(hn0, hn1)
    df      AIC
hn0  1 192.3058
hn1  2 193.3776

> AIC(hr0, hr1)
    df      AIC
hr0  2 191.5479
hr1  3 193.5481

As you can see, "hr0" model is selected in both procedures, but I'm not sure which one is -statistically- more correct. 

Pd. If you are wondering why my CTDS is not overdispersed, I could say that is a consequence of the relatively low number of distances recorded to each individual.  On average, I have only 6 distances for each animal. It was a small species (low probability of detection for the CTs) that crossed relatively fast the detection zone (low number of detections despite snapshot gap is 1sec)

Thanks a lot for your help :)

Cheers 
Pablo

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] c-hat value and model selection
parts:
Pablo

I'm not sure, as you note, there is a distinction between the two model selection routes in this instance; primarily because of the small c-hat values. If I were writing this up, I would present the argument you have done in your email: c-hat is small, hence the two forms of model selection converge upon the same model choice. Subsequent to the presentation of the c-hat values, you could argue that the most parsimonious procedure would be the classic.

Recall Howe et al. (2019) developed an alternative procedure to solve a particular problem. That problem does not seem to exist in your data set.
